blockContainer.p: Rules on granting financial assistance to beneficiaries under the common fisheries policy (CFP) are set out in Regulation (EU) No 1380/2013 (‘CFP Regulation’), Article 42 of which provides that ‘Union financial assistance to operators shall be conditional upon compliance with the CFP rules by operators'.

Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1139 on the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (‘EMFAF Regulation’) lays down rules on the admissibility of applications submitted by operators. The following cases trigger inadmissibility:

item.p: serious infringements of the rules of the CFP, as provided for in Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008 (‘IUU Regulation’) and Regulation (EC) No 1224/2009 (‘Control Regulation’),

involvement in the operation, management or ownership of a fishing vessel included in the Union IUU (‘illegal, unreported, unregulated’) vessel list, or of a vessel flying the flag of countries identified as non-cooperating third countries,
as regards aquaculture, environmental offences set out in Articles 3 and 4 of Directive 2008/99/EC on the protection of the environment through criminal law,
fraud in the context of the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund (EMFF) or the EMFAF.

blockContainer.p: Under Article 11 of the EMFAF Regulation, these inadmissibility arrangements must ‘be proportionate to the nature, gravity, duration and repetition of the serious infringements’

For this purpose, the EMFAF Regulation empowers the Commission to adopt a delegated act establishing: (a) the threshold above which applications by operators who have committed serious infringements, environmental offences or fraud are no longer admissible; (b) the duration of the period of inadmissibility that shall be at least of one year’ duration, including its starting and ending dates and the conditions for reducing it; and (c) the arrangements for recovering the aid granted under financial corrections by Member States.

Serious infringements of the CFP cause grave harm to fishing resources and the marine environment. Such infringements include e.g. fishing without a valid licence, using prohibited gear, falsifying markings, identity or registration, and manipulating an engine with the aim of increasing its power beyond the maximum continuous engine power according to the engine certificate. Pursuant to Article 90(1) of the Control Regulation, Member States determine if an infringement qualifies as ‘serious’, taking into account criteria such as the nature of the damage, the value of the damage, the economic situation of the offender and the extent of the infringement or its repetition.

tblock.heading: CONSULTATIONS PRIOR TO THE ADOPTION OF THE ACT

blockContainer.p: Member States were consulted on the content of the draft delegated act on 11 May 2022 through an EMFAF Expert Group. They were invited to submit their observations and share their experience with admissibility rules under the EMFF.

tblock.heading: LEGAL ELEMENTS OF THE DELEGATED ACT

blockContainer.p: The provisions on the admissibility of applications under the EMFAF are very close to those established in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2015/288 on the admissibility of applications under the EMFF.

As regards the threshold triggering inadmissibility, the delegated act is based upon the number of serious infringements, environmental offences or fraud committed by the operator. In the case of serious infringements of the rules of the CFP, the delegated act takes into account the gravity and seriousness of the case by modulating the threshold based upon the number of infringements points assigned to the operator pursuant to Annex XXX to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 404/2011.

The duration of inadmissibility is in principle 12 months, which is the minimum required by Article 11 of the EMFAF Regulation. The delegated act takes into account the repetition of serious infringements by extending that duration if additional serious infringements are committed during the period of inadmissibility.
The delegated act also establishes rules as regards operators that own or control more than one fishing vessel, and rules on transfer of ownership of fishing vessels.
